name: Mucinous cystadenoma of childhood

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and radiological diagnostic criteria for mucinous cystadenoma

criteria.description: Presence of multilocular cystic ovarian tumor lined by mucin-producing epithelial cells without stromal invasion
Ultrasound or MRI showing large multilocular cystic ovarian mass with thin septations and absence of solid nodules
Presentation in childhood or adolescence with ovarian mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mucinous cystadenoma with supportive imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Exclusion of malignant features and other cystic ovarian neoplasms is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to ovarian cyst

searchTerms: mild pain or fullness below stomach

common.symptomName: Urinary frequency due to mass effect
searchTerms: frequent urination caused by pelvic mass
increased bathroom trips due to pressure

occasional.symptomName: Acute abdominal pain from cyst rupture or torsion
searchTerms: sudden belly pain from cyst burst or twist
acute abdominal pain from cyst complications
sharp stomach pain due to cyst rupture or torsion
gaining weight due to cyst size
body weight rise from cyst volume
difficulty passing stool due to mass
hydronephrosis due to urine flow obstruction

laboratory: Normal tumor markers (CA-125 usually normal or mildly elevated)
Normal complete blood count and metabolic panel
imaging: Ultrasound showing large multilocular cystic ovarian mass with thin septations
MRI confirming cystic nature without solid enhancing components
genetic: Somatic mutations rare and not well characterized
other: Histopathology demonstrating mucin-producing epithelial lining without stromal invasion
Absence of malignant features such as cellular atypia or stromal invasion

distinguishingFeatures: Serous cystadenomas typically have clear serous fluid rather than mucinous content
Histology shows ciliated columnar epithelium instead of mucinous epithelium
Presence of stromal invasion and cellular atypia on histology
Solid nodules or papillary projections on imaging

redFlags: Severe acute abdominal pain suggestive of cyst rupture or torsion
Signs of malignancy such as weight loss or ascites
references: Orphanet: Mucinous cystadenoma of childhood - ORPHA:563671
Young RH. Ovarian mucinous tumors in children and adolescents. Int J Gynecol Pathol. 2014
WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs, 5th Edition, 2020
